chunks: Those who are blessed will be in Paradise, where they will dwell so long as heaven and earth survive, unless your Lord wills otherwise: This will be a gift uninterrupted.
ai.seo_question: How long will the blessed remain in Paradise according to Surah Hud?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is central to the debate on whether Paradise is eternal or temporary, with the majority of scholars affirming its permanence for the blessed based on the phrase 'unless your Lord wills.' The term 'non-exhaustible gift' (ata'an ghayra majdhoodin) highlights the infinite nature of divine grace, distinguishing it from finite worldly rewards. This interpretation aligns with the Shia view of God's mercy as boundless, reinforcing the theological certainty of eternal bliss for the righteous.
